clue.text: Member of Foreign Office advocates abandoning of peace initiative

parts.note: FO is the standard abbreviation for the British Foreign Office
to rearm is to arm again, the policy of those who would give up on peace efforts

explanation.surface: A diplomat at the Foreign Office calls for an end to a peace drive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Member' is a limb here, not a member of staff; the long phrase is a loose description of re-arming.
explanation.definitionFit: The lower arm is a limb, and a limb is a bodily member.

clue.text: Worry about a proverb that cuts across the grain

parts.note: to fret is to worry
a saw is an old saying or proverb

explanation.surface: Someone frets over a saying that goes against the usual way of thinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Against the grain' suggests contrarian thinking, but the definition is literal woodwork: this fine saw cuts curves across wood.
explanation.definitionFit: This narrow-bladed saw is used for cutting intricate curves in wood, often across the grain.

clue.text: Get better binding for the book

definitions.meaning: read as ..., giving a book a fresh cover

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is to regain health; the other, split as re-cover, is to put a new cover on a book.

clue.text: Otto makes a mince tart

indicators.note: to mince is to chop up finely, so these letters are cut and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone called Otto bakes a mince tart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Otto' looks like a man's name but is a variant of 'ottar', the perfume oil; 'mince' poses as pie filling.
explanation.definitionFit: Otto is an old variant name for the fragrant essential oil distilled from rose petals.

clue.text: Two graduates and I join American girls for unaccompanied songs

parts.note: MA, Master of Arts, is one graduate's degree
DR, doctor, is the second graduate
gals is an American colloquial word for girls

explanation.surface: Two university graduates and the speaker team up with some American girls to sing unaccompanied.
explanation.definitionFit: These part-songs of the Renaissance were sung by several voices without instruments.

clue.text: One who takes steps to make his protest public?

definitions.text: One who takes steps to make his protest public?

parts.words: One who takes steps to make his protest public?
parts.note: taking steps sounds like starting a procedure, but literally means walking in a demonstration

explanation.definitionFit: A demonstrator who walks in a protest procession is a participant on the march.

clue.text: Chiseller provides for one parent family

parts.note: ma is a familiar word for mother, one parent
a son is part of one's family, one's offspring

explanation.surface: A con man supports a single-parent household.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chiseller' suggests a swindler, but it is literal: a stoneworker who uses a chisel.
explanation.definitionFit: A stonecutter shapes blocks with a chisel, so he is literally a chiseller.

clue.text: Withdrew from area of land surrounded by marsh weed

indicators.note: the stretch of land is enclosed within the plant's letters, as it would be in a reed bed

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass growing in marshes
a tract is an expanse of land

explanation.surface: Someone pulled out of a plot of land overgrown with marsh plants.
explanation.definitionFit: To take back a statement or claw is to draw it back, to withdraw it.

clue.text: One of the Marx brothers performing as a prelude to blubbering

parts.note: Harpo was the silent, harp-playing Marx brother of film comedy
on means on stage, performing

explanation.surface: One of the Marx Brothers is on stage, about to burst into tears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blubbering' suggests weeping, but it is whaling: a harpoon comes before getting the blubber.
explanation.definitionFit: A whaler's barbed spear is thrown first, before the whale's fat can be stripped.

clue.text: Book describing shyness

definitions.meaning: to book is to make a reservation

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is to book ahead; the other is reticence, a reluctance to show feelings.

clue.text: Worked up case naming former spouse as co-respondent?

parts.note: ex is a former husband or wife
to cite someone in a divorce case is to name them as co-respondent

explanation.surface: Someone is agitated at a divorce case naming their former partner as the third party.
explanation.walkthrough: A co-respondent is the person accused of adultery with the respondent in a divorce; to cite them is to name them in the case.
explanation.definitionFit: Being worked up means being agitated, stirred and full of feeling.

clue.text: Salvation Army becomes weary of parodies

parts.note: tires means grows weary

explanation.surface: The Salvation Army grows tired of mockery.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are works that ridicule their targets by exaggeration and mockery.

clue.text: Though worth four crowns he has only one

definitions.text: Though worth four crowns he has only one

parts.words: Though worth four crowns he has only one
parts.note: an old British gold coin worth twenty shillings equalled four five-shilling crowns, while a monarch wears just one crown

explanation.walkthrough: A crown was an old British coin worth five shillings, a quarter of a pound.
explanation.definitionFit: The old gold pound coin was worth four crowns, and a monarch wears a single crown.

clue.text: Affair in which I claim to be possessive of us

parts.note: saying I am is claiming to be something
our is the possessive form of us

explanation.surface: A lover in a relationship claims to be possessive of the couple.
explanation.definitionFit: A love affair, often a secret one, is what the French word for love denotes in English.

clue.text: Word encompassing Latin "terra"

indicators.note: the letters of Word wrap round the abbreviation, holding it inside

explanation.surface: A dictionary entry explains the Latin term for earth.
explanation.definitionFit: Terra is Latin for earth, the globe we live on.

clue.text: Transvestite attire?

parts.note: a man's formal tailcoat, jokingly read as clothing for a man who wears dresses

explanation.definitionFit: A man's formal evening tailcoat is named as if it were cross-dressing gear.

clue.text: Suddenly everyone acts simultaneously

definitions.meaning: the whole group doing something together at the same moment

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means abruptly, and also literally every person at one time.

clue.text: A peer could on the other hand be merely a civic dignitary

parts.note: a lord is a peer of the realm
may expresses possibility, like could
or introduces an alternative

explanation.surface: A nobleman might, alternatively, be only a town official.
explanation.walkthrough: The head of a city council in London and other big British cities bears this title, though he need not be a peer.
explanation.definitionFit: The head of certain city corporations is a ceremonial civic official.

clue.text: He who takes over a victory by common soldiers

parts.note: a success is a win or triumph
OR, other ranks, means soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: A new leader owes victory to the rank and file.
explanation.definitionFit: An heir or replacement follows another person in an office or role.

clue.text: Coast or resort for a tourist in the Indian Ocean

definitions.text: for a tourist in the Indian Ocean

indicators.note: read as re-sort, sorting the letters again into a new order

explanation.surface: A tourist chooses between the coast and a holiday resort in the Indian Ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resort' looks like a holiday spot but is the anagram signal, re-sort.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an island off the Horn of Africa, a destination in that ocean.

clue.text: The cost of waiting for wine

definitions.text: The cost of waiting for wine

parts.words: The cost of waiting for wine
parts.note: waiting means serving as a waiter, not hanging about: a restaurant fee for serving a bottle the diner brought

explanation.definitionFit: A restaurant charges this fee for opening and serving a bottle brought by the customer.

clue.text: Badge designed to humiliate

indicators.note: designed suggests something made over, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A badge is made to shame its wearer.
explanation.walkthrough: To debag is old British student slang for pulling someone's trousers off as a prank.
explanation.definitionFit: Removing someone's trousers as a prank is done to embarrass and shame them.

clue.text: Mistake a flower

definitions.meaning: read as ..., a plant that blooms

explanation.definitionFit: It is British slang for a blunder, and literally means a plant that blooms.

clue.text: New angle top journalist managed to pick up

indicators.note: a new version of the word, its letters rearranged

parts.note: ED, editor, is the senior journalist

explanation.surface: A fresh angle was what the editor managed to grasp.
explanation.definitionFit: Gathering bit by bit, like collecting leftover grain, is picking up information.

clue.text: Centres of carbon and mineral deposits

parts.note: C is the chemical symbol for carbon
ores are mineral deposits mined for metal

explanation.surface: The heart of a seam of coal and mineral deposits.
explanation.definitionFit: The central parts of things, like the middle of an apple.

clue.text: Was Limehouse built ofit?

parts.note: the London district's name is read as if it were a house made of a particular rock

explanation.walkthrough: Limehouse is a district of East London.
explanation.definitionFit: This sedimentary rock is a common building stone, and the place name begins with its first part.

clue.text: Light cutting instrument

parts.note: read as a device that cuts with light, not a lightweight cutter

explanation.definitionFit: This device produces a focused beam that can slice through materials.

clue.text: Brace-one's shoulders back when walking?

definitions.meaning: a support or prop in a framework
to walk proudly and stiffly with chest out

explanation.definitionFit: It is a supporting bar in a structure, and also a swaggering way of walking.

clue.text: Vessels intended for leaving Italian river in frightful state

indicators.note: the river's letters go inside the jumbled word
something frightful is a mess, so these letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: the Po is the longest river in Italy

explanation.surface: Ships bound to leave an Italian river in a terrible condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'frightful' rearranges the word state, and 'in' sets the river inside. 'leaving' seems to mean departing, but the definition puns on tea leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: Pots for brewing tea are vessels meant for tea leaves.

clue.text: Maybe detective posing as a senior farm hand

definitions.meaning: a man from Scotland Yard, London's police headquarters, for example a detective
a worker in charge of a farmyard

explanation.walkthrough: Scotland Yard is the headquarters of London's Metropolitan Police.
explanation.definitionFit: It can mean a Scotland Yard officer, or a labourer who tends the farmyard.

clue.text: A more satisfactory accomplice

parts.note: better means more satisfactory

explanation.surface: A partner in crime who does the job better.
explanation.definitionFit: One who aids or encourages a wrongdoer is an accomplice.

clue.text: No longer working but unlikely to get a flat

definitions.meaning: having stopped work in old age
read as re-tyred, fitted with new tyres, so less likely to suffer a puncture

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is having stopped working for good; the other, split as re-tyred, means freshly fitted wheels.
